request.spec:
A steward can move a DRAFT, OPEN or PENDING claim to another person on the sheet (a refusal shows an
error on the claim). The claim keeps its number and date, loses any figure a statement bound it to
(it is live again until its new person's next statement), every total follows, and CLAIM_REASSIGNED
is written, naming the claim like every claim line (with the new person) and ending from=<old name>
to=<new name>. A settled or voided claim cannot move. The moved claim is listed as its new person's
newest claim (first under them), whatever its date.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A steward can now move a DRAFT, OPEN or PENDING claim to another person on the sheet. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests (the main reassign test and three scenarios).

**How it behaves**
- Each claim row has a person picker (`claim-reassign-to`, listing everyone except the claim's current person) and a Reassign button (`claim-reassign`).
- The move is refused, with `claim-error` shown and nothing written, if:
  - the user isn't a steward,
  - the claim is SETTLED or VOID,
  - the chosen person isn't another person on the sheet,
  - or another user changed the claim's person or status since it was read.
- A moved claim keeps its number and date. It loses any figure a statement bound it to, so its due is live again at the new person's rate.
- The audit gets `CLAIM_REASSIGNED … person=<new> amount=… date=… [number=…] from=<old> to=<new>`. Moving an open claim also writes ROLLUP lines for both people and a TOTALS line. Moving a draft writes none, because drafts don't count toward totals.

**Server**
- New endpoint `POST /api/sheets/{sheet}/claims/{claim}/reassign` with body `{"to": <personId>}`, made of the steps `ValidateReassign` → `LoadClaim` → `ReassignClaim` → `RespondWithClaims`.
- `Claims.reassign` changes the person, clears the statement binding and moves the claim to the top of the list in one update. The update only applies if the claim still has the person and status it was read with.

**Listing order (the one design choice to know about)**
Claims used to be listed newest-first by id. But the id is part of each row's `data-testid`, so I couldn't give a moved claim a new id to put it at the top. Instead, migration `V23__claim_listed.sql` adds a `listed` column (existing claims get `listed = id`). A claim takes the sheet's next `listed` value when it's added and again when it's reassigned, and the list is sorted by `listed DESC, id DESC`. This puts a moved claim first under its new person whatever its date, and claims added later still list above it.

**Front end**
The picker, button and error are in `features/claims/claims.slot.tsx`. A reassign error clears on the row's next action, and the row's other errors clear when you reassign.
